teams.heading: Jake White hails Fiji as rugby's 'Harlem Globetrotters' and predicts World Cup improvement
teams.body: Speaking after Friday's 23-21 defeat by Italy at Twickenham, White described his squad as “the Harlem Globetrotters of world rugby” and said his task is to blend that flair with lessons from coaching in South Africa, France, Japan and at the Brumbies. His first fixes are stopping mauls and building a scrum that stops conceding penalties. That is pointed, given a scrum penalty set up Tommaso Allan's winning kick. He predicted Fiji will be much better by next October's World Cup in Australia, citing a two-and-a-half-month training camp.

lead.why: Fiji's coach setting out his project and World Cup outlook is the freshest Fiji story not already run.

teams.heading: Sam Warburton hails Borthwick's Itoje sabbatical call as 'a stroke of genius'
teams.body: Writing in The Times, the former Lions captain credited Borthwick with suggesting the break that kept Itoje out of July's Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina. That gave a lock who had not had a full pre-season in more than a decade time away from the international grind. “Maro has simply been on fire this autumn.” Warburton pointed to the 37-12 pool win over New Zealand, in which Itoje made 49 ruck entries. Ollie Chessum was next highest with 31.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby backs Galthié's all-Bordeaux front-row to beat Springboks in final

Planet Rugby reads it as a side picked to win the collisions and breakdown before a powerful bench finishes the job. It also says South Africa, shorn of Pieter-Steph du Toit, need a perfect storm. A fortnight ago in Paris, France scored three first-half tries to lead 21-7 before hanging on to win 21-19.

teams.heading: Nick Timoney praises Ireland's instant rebound in 215-tackle win over Wallabies
teams.body: Friday's 38-14 win at Twickenham began with Australia holding more than 90% possession before Jeremy Williams burrowed over for a 7-0 lead. Robbie Henshaw's try levelled it within minutes. "That's massive," Timoney said of the instant reply, adding: "It didn't come all that naturally." Ireland made 215 tackles to the Wallabies' 129. From 11 entries to the 22 apiece, Andy Farrell's side scored five tries and a penalty, while Les Kiss's men were limited to two tries.

teams.heading: Tommaso Menoncello to have shoulder surgery, likely out of Italy's Six Nations
teams.body: The Toulouse centre's shoulder gave way again in training, leaving no option but an operation. He first damaged it in a mid-October Champions Cup tie against Exeter, an acromioclavicular sprain. After a month and a half of conservative treatment he was back in training and looked close to playing. OnRugby puts the lay-off at three to four months. Even on the shortest timeline he would return in late February or early March without match minutes, which it judges too late to risk for the closing rounds.

lead.why: A fresh injury to a key Italy centre outranks a win the reader saw yesterday.

teams.heading: Finn Russell returns at fly-half as Townsend makes 11 changes for Argentina
teams.body: Rory Darge is back from injury to captain the side, with only four starters from the 67-5 rout of Japan keeping their places, Jamie Dobie among them at scrum-half inside the returning Russell. With the squad's number eights injured, Magnus Bradbury gets his chance in the back row; Townsend called it "a big opportunity for him ahead of the Six Nations." Rory Hutchinson starts at 12, forming a centre pairing with Huw Jones that the coach likens to Sione Tuipulotu and Jones.

teams.heading: Jac Morgan scores twice off the bench as Wales beat Japan 40-10
teams.body: Wales closed their Nations Championship with six tries at Twickenham in the ninth-place final. Josh Adams crossed twice, with Blair Murray and Reuben Morgan-Williams, on his first start, also scoring as Steve Tandy's side led by 26 points at the break; the replacement flanker added his pair after half-time. Sam Costelow landed five conversions. Ellis Mee started on the wing after Louis Rees-Zammit was withdrawn with illness just over an hour before kick-off, and James Botham made 38 tackles.

teams.body: The Zebre fullback, a mainstay of Argentina's sevens side, has no Test caps and could debut off the bench in the seventh-place final against Scotland at Twickenham. That final is a rematch of July's 47-38 defeat in Córdoba. Picking Wade means Matías Moroni misses the chance to win a 100th Pumas cap. Elsewhere, Rodrigo Martínez replaces the injured Boris Wenger in the front row, and 22-year-old Faustino Sánchez Valarolo partners Lucio Cinti in midfield.

teams.heading: BBC's Mike Henson warns All Blacks' 2026 slump nears 1949 low
teams.body: Writing before Saturday's Twickenham rematch, the BBC's rugby union news reporter set out how loose the All Blacks' grip has become: defeat would be a sixth in a calendar year, a total matched only once before — in 1949, when a split squad played two Test series at once in Australia and South Africa. New Zealand's 2026 win percentage of 58.3% is the third lowest of the professional era, and Henson asks whether the in-house coaching succession from Graham Henry through Steve Hansen to Ian Foster has turned against them.

lead.why: The strongest new New Zealand story; Umaga and fatigue have already run, and Steward is England's story.

teams.heading: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu moves to full-back to make way for Manie Libbok
teams.body: Libbok, who came off the bench against Italy and France before missing the squad for last weekend's defeat to Ireland, partners Cobus Reinach at half-back in Sunday's Nations Championship final against France. His former Stormers teammate had been first-choice fly-half in all three of those Tests and now joins Ethan Hooker and Kurt-Lee Arendse in the back three. The 29-year-old trusts the understanding: "We know each other really well and we are familiar with one another’s game, so we feed off each other well."
